questions.q: What are the three panels of the Pit workspace?
questions.correct: Lessons, the code editor, and a 3D test stand
wrong: Lessons, the code editor, and a match scoreboard
A code editor, a chat window, and a scoreboard
Lessons, a video player, and a spare parts catalog
questions.explain: The Pit has three panels: the lessons on the left, the code editor top-right, and a 3D test-stand preview bottom-right. You read, code, and see the result all in one place.

questions.q: What is the basic development loop in the Pit?
questions.correct: Edit the code, Build & Init, then Run
wrong: Run the code, then edit it, then delete it
Build first, then write the code, then delete
Import a file, then print it, then unplug it
questions.explain: The core cycle is Edit → Build & Init → Run. You change the code, press Build & Init to compile and load it, then Start to run it and watch what happens.

questions.q: What does the Build & Init button do?
questions.correct: Compiles your code and loads it onto the robot
wrong: Deletes your code and starts a brand-new file
Runs the program immediately without any compiling
Exports your whole package as a zip download
questions.explain: Build & Init compiles your Java and loads it onto the robot (the INIT step). After that, Start actually runs the program and Stop halts it.

questions.correct: A personal folder of your Java files in the browser
wrong: A single line of code copied from the lesson
A zip file the robot mails to the judges
A physical box holding robot parts and wires
questions.explain: A code package is your own folder of Java files, saved in the browser. You can make several, switch between them, and export or import them as a .zip.

questions.q: How do you save a code package to share or back up?
questions.correct: Export it as a .zip file you can download
wrong: Print it on paper and scan it back later
Email the robot a screenshot of the code
Leave it open and hope the tab stays alive
questions.explain: Packages export as a .zip you can download, and you can import a .zip back in. That's how you back up or share your work between computers.

questions.correct: Puts your code back to this lesson's starting point
wrong: Deletes every single package you have ever made
Marks the current lesson as fully complete
Uploads your code to the competition server
questions.explain: Reset Lesson Code restores the files to how they should look at the START of the lesson, so you can begin fresh. It does overwrite your current edits.

questions.q: What runs the program after you press Start?
questions.correct: Start runs the loaded code, and Stop halts it
wrong: Start compiles the code, and Stop deletes the code
Start opens the editor, and Stop closes the browser
Start charges the battery, and Stop drains it
questions.explain: After Build & Init loads your code, Start runs it and Stop halts it. It's the run/halt half of the Edit → Build → Run loop.

questions.q: Why does the starter code begin so minimal?
questions.correct: Starting simple keeps things clear as features get added
wrong: The robot cannot store more than a few lines
Long programs are against the FTC competition rules
A shorter file makes the battery last much longer
questions.explain: The starter is intentionally bare so nothing is confusing at first. You add features one lesson at a time, and each addition stays easy to follow.

questions.q: Does the robot already know how to drive when you start?
questions.correct: No — it knows its hardware but has no driving code yet
wrong: Yes — it drives itself perfectly from the very start
Yes — but only during the 30-second autonomous period
No — and it can never be taught to drive at all
questions.explain: The robot knows about its motors and gamepad, but you haven't told it what to DO yet. Writing those instructions is the whole point of the lessons.

questions.q: How do you work on more than one program at once?
questions.correct: Make several packages and switch with the dropdown
wrong: Only one package can ever exist at a time
Open a second browser on another computer
Rename the same one file over and over again
questions.explain: The "+ Package" button makes new packages, and a dropdown selector switches between them. Each is its own separate folder of files.

questions.q: Where do you see messages from your running program?
questions.correct: On the telemetry your code prints to the Driver Hub
wrong: Only in a printout the robot mails you later
Nowhere at all — running code is totally silent
Inside the battery's own tiny status screen
questions.explain: Programs report what they're doing through telemetry, shown on the Driver Hub screen. It's your main window into what the code is really doing.

questions.q: What is the test stand in the Pit for?
questions.correct: Previewing your robot's mechanisms in 3D as they run
wrong: Charging the real robot's battery between matches
Storing spare motors and servos for a later build
Scoring the match and showing the final points
questions.explain: The bottom-right test-stand panel shows a 3D preview of the robot so you can watch mechanisms move as your code runs, without needing the field.

questions.q: After you change code, what must happen before it runs?
questions.correct: You Build & Init so the new code compiles and loads
wrong: Nothing at all — edits run live as you type
You must fully restart the whole computer first
You export a zip and email it to yourself
questions.explain: Edits don't take effect until you Build & Init, which compiles the new code and loads it. Then Start runs the updated version.

questions.q: What happens when you press Stop?
questions.correct: It halts the program that is running on the robot
wrong: It permanently erases your whole code package
It compiles the code into a brand-new file
It marks the current lesson as complete for you
questions.explain: Stop halts the program that's currently running. It doesn't touch your code — you can edit, Build & Init, and Start again.

questions.q: Which panel shows the lessons you work through?
questions.correct: The left panel of the Pit workspace
wrong: The bottom-right test-stand preview panel
The top-right code editor panel area
A separate pop-up window each single time
questions.explain: The lessons live in the left panel. The editor is top-right and the 3D test stand is bottom-right, so you can read, code, and watch all at once.
